🔻 Israel violates Gaza ceasefire 4,803 times, killing 1,369 Palestinians: Report

📌 Tehran, IRNA - Israeli occupation forces committed 24 new violations of the ceasefire agreement in the Gaza Strip over 24 hours ending Friday, bringing the total number of recorded violations to 4,803 since the agreement came into force 335 days ago, according to a daily monitoring report.

The report, which documents violations through figures and field developments, said that one Palestinian was martyred and 28 others were wounded in the latest Israeli attacks.  The cumulative death toll since the ceasefire began now stands at 1,369, while the total number of wounded has reached 4,627.
​
Children, women, and the elderly account for a disproportionate share of the casualties. According to the data, 474 of the martyrs, 34.6 percent, were children, women, or elderly persons. Among the wounded, 2,278, or 49.2 percent, fall into those same categories.
​
The report also noted that 191 Palestinians have been detained since the agreement took effect, with no new detentions recorded in the latest 24-hour period.
​
It also documented continued Israeli non-compliance with the humanitarian provisions of the ceasefire agreement, which stipulate the entry of 600 trucks per day, including 50 fuel trucks.
​
Field data confirmed that only 210.6 trucks per day have entered on average, just 35.1 percent of the agreed amount. The shortfall was most severe for fuel deliveries, which reached only 15.6 percent of the agreed quota. Aid trucks accounted for 49.1 percent of actual entries, commercial trucks for 47.1 percent, and fuel trucks for just 3.7 percent.
​
The report said occupation authorities continue to provide misleading figures to mediators and refuse independent international monitoring.
​
Rafah crossing remains obstructed
​
The report also detailed continued violations at the Rafah crossing, where Israeli forces have imposed arbitrary and degrading procedures and severely reduced the number of permitted crossings, including for humanitarian and medical cases that were agreed to be facilitated.
​
The actual number of travelers moving through the crossing in both directions reached 12,931 out of 34,800 individuals scheduled to travel, a compliance rate of 39.4 percent. A total of 91 individuals were turned back at the crossing.
​
The report noted that it does not reiterate previous violations that remain unresolved, particularly breaches of agreed withdrawal lines, the imposition of armed control over approximately 34 square kilometers outside the scope of the agreement, and non-compliance with the humanitarian protocol.
​
These also include obstruction of urgent infrastructure repairs such as electricity, water, and sewage networks, prevention of heavy machinery entry, continued exposure of detainees to torture and inhuman treatment, and ongoing lack of clarity regarding the fate of the missing.
​
“All in all, the data demonstrates that the violations committed by the occupation forces constitute a continuous and systematic pattern that has struck at the core of the agreement and stripped its procedures of their practical substance,” the report concluded.
​
“These findings underscore the urgent need for serious international action to ensure an end to the violations and the protection of civilians.”

If you're still here, I want you to read this.
ㅤ
Yes. YOU.
ㅤ
The person who has spent years wondering if you're the only one who sees that something isn't right.
ㅤ
The person who stopped talking about certain things at family dinners because you got tired of the arguments.
ㅤ
The person who lost friends because you refused to pretend you believed something you didn't.
ㅤ
The person who was called crazy.
ㅤ
Conspiracy theorist.
ㅤ
Extremist.
ㅤ
Dangerous.
ㅤ
Selfish.
ㅤ
Uneducated.
ㅤ
You heard it all.
ㅤ
And sometimes, when nobody was around, you probably asked yourself:
ㅤ
“What if I’m wrong?”
ㅤ
But instead of giving up, you kept searching.
ㅤ
You read.
ㅤ
You listened.
ㅤ
You questioned BOTH sides.
ㅤ
You changed your mind when the evidence demanded it.
ㅤ
And most importantly…
ㅤ
You refused to hand your ability to think over to somebody else.
ㅤ
That takes more courage than people realize.
ㅤ
Because standing with a crowd is easy.
ㅤ
Standing alone?
ㅤ
That's different.
ㅤ
Some of you paid a real price.
ㅤ
Friendships disappeared.
ㅤ
Families became divided.
ㅤ
People you loved stopped speaking to you.
ㅤ
Some of you learned the painful lesson that certain people only accepted you when you agreed with them.
ㅤ
And yet somehow…
ㅤ
YOUR HEART DIDN'T TURN TO STONE.
ㅤ
You still care.
ㅤ
You still pray for people who would never pray for you.
ㅤ
You still want a better future for children who aren't even yours.
ㅤ
You still look at this broken world and believe it can be saved.
ㅤ
Think about that.
ㅤ
After everything you've seen…
ㅤ
YOU STILL HAVE HOPE.
ㅤ
Never underestimate how powerful that is.
ㅤ
You don't need millions of followers.
ㅤ
You don't need to become famous.
ㅤ
You don't need to win every argument.
ㅤ
You don't even need everyone to understand you.
ㅤ
Just keep your eyes open.
ㅤ
Keep asking questions.
ㅤ
Keep your family close.
ㅤ
Help people when you can.
ㅤ
Admit when you're wrong.
ㅤ
Stand firm when you know you're right.
ㅤ
And above everything else…
ㅤ
KEEP GOD FIRST.
ㅤ
Because this battle was never only political.
ㅤ
It's a battle over fear.
ㅤ
Truth.
ㅤ
Faith.
ㅤ
Family.
ㅤ
And what kind of world we're going to leave behind.
ㅤ
So if nobody has told you lately:
ㅤ
I'm glad you're still here.
ㅤ
I'm glad you didn't give up.
ㅤ
I'm glad you're still searching.
ㅤ
I'm glad you still care.
ㅤ
And somewhere out there, someone else needs to know they're not alone either.
ㅤ
Send this to them.
ㅤ
Keep your head up.
ㅤ
Keep your faith stronger than your fear.
ㅤ
We may not know what tomorrow brings…
ㅤ
BUT GOD DOES. 🙏🇺🇸
ㅤ
If this message hit home, don't keep it to yourself.
ㅤ
Share it with someone who needs to hear it today.
ㅤ
You're not alone. And you're not done. 🇺🇸

🔻 Minab school massacre symbolizes oppression inflicted on Iran: Minister

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Minister of Culture and Islamic Guidance Abbas Salehi has described the Minab school tragedy as a symbol of oppression inflicted on Iran, saying its international resonance could help deter future unjust wars.

Speaking at a ceremony on Monday, Salehi said the Minab school massacre stands out among many other tragic events of the past 50 years because of its unique characteristics and should not be allowed to become a memory buried in the past.
​
He added that, unlike some similar incidents, the Minab school tragedy gained widespread global resonance because it occurred on the first day of the war.
​
Salehi stressed that the Minab massacre could serve as the flag of oppression inflicted on Iran at the international level and have a deterrent effect against unjust wars.
​
